subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw treat its shipped abort-and-immediate-contextual-next-turn behavior as sufficient soft steering, or add a resumable checkpoint lifecycle for partial model and tool execution?
rationale: Current OpenClaw and Codex contracts provide distinct boundary steering and turn interruption; transparent pause-and-resume would be a materially new cross-runtime state-management guarantee.

options.title: Standardize interrupt mode
options.body: Use the shipped abort-and-new-turn behavior as the supported course-correction contract and resolve the stale implementation PR.

options.title: Build resumable checkpoints
options.body: Sponsor a larger paused-run state machine with explicit partial output, tool side-effect, cancellation, and restoration semantics.

options.title: Retain boundary steering only
options.body: Keep steer boundary-oriented and document that immediate interruption requires selecting interrupt mode.

recommendation.title: Standardize interrupt mode
recommendation.body: Use the shipped abort-and-new-turn behavior as the supported course-correction contract and resolve the stale implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and consolidated the queue behavior and already supplied product-level review context for this issue.
